_meta.authored_by: initial draft from corpus knowledge — REQUIRES OWNER REVIEW
notes: Schema v2 change: every rule (include_if / exclude_if / match_boost_if) carries its OWN source (filename, page, note) so the structured layer is auditable at the criterion level.

`applicability_rules` (renamed from `include_if`) — every rule must be satisfied by the user's attributes for the scheme to be POTENTIALLY APPLICABLE. Missing user attributes (value == 'unknown') do not fail rules — they are noted in `missing_information` instead.
`disqualifying_rules` — if ANY rule fires against explicit user attributes, the scheme is dropped. Missing user attributes do NOT disqualify.
`match_boost_if` — soft signals that raise a scheme in the ranking without gating inclusion.
`required_information` — attributes the user MUST provide before a definitive eligibility judgement is possible. Missing entries are surfaced to the user as 'we still need to know X'.
`always_include` — for schemes that apply to essentially every farmer (PM-KISAN, KCC, PMFBY). Included when the user gave no explicit attributes at all.

Language contract: this file NEVER states 'the farmer is eligible'. Downstream code renders 'potentially applicable based on what you told me' and lists both provided_information and missing_information.
Owner: edit any factual line here and the discovery layer reflects it on next restart. No re-embed needed.

schemes.name: PM-KISAN
schemes.one_liner: Direct income support of ₹6,000 per year to all landholding farmer families, paid in three ₹2,000 installments.

source.note: Landholding farmer families are eligible for PM-KISAN.
Income tax payers in the last assessment year are excluded.
Serving / retired Group A & B govt employees are excluded.

required_information.why_needed: PM-KISAN applies to landholding farmer families — we need to know that the user owns cultivable land.
Farmer families paying income tax in the last AY are excluded.
Serving / retired Group A & B govt employees are excluded.

key_benefits: ₹6,000 per year direct benefit transfer to the farmer family
Paid in three equal installments of ₹2,000 every four months
Aadhaar-seeded direct bank transfer
schemes.who_should_apply: Landholding farmer families whose cultivable land is in their name — subject to standard exclusions for income tax payers, Group A/B govt employees, and professionals.

how_to_register.in_person: Local Common Service Centre (CSC) or State Nodal Officer

schemes.follow_up_query_hint: How do I register on the PM-KISAN portal?

schemes.name: PMFBY
schemes.one_liner: Crop insurance covering yield losses from natural calamities, pests, and disease. Farmer premium share is capped low; the balance is paid by centre and state.

source.note: PMFBY covers all food & oilseed crops and annual commercial/horticultural crops for which past yield data are available.

required_information.why_needed: PMFBY covers notified crops only — we need to know what the user grows to confirm the crop is notified in their district.
Enrolment is compulsory for loanee (SAO/KCC) farmers and voluntary for non-loanee farmers; the process differs.
Some crops are notified only in specific states — geography matters for PMFBY.

key_benefits: Farmer premium share: 2% for Kharif food-grain and oilseed crops
Farmer premium share: 1.5% for Rabi food-grain and oilseed crops
Farmer premium share: 5% for annual commercial/horticultural crops
Mandatory for loanee farmers (SAO/KCC borrowers); voluntary for non-loanee farmers
Covers all food & oilseed crops and annual commercial/horticultural crops
schemes.who_should_apply: Loanee farmers (auto-enrolled through banks) and non-loanee farmers with insurable interest in notified crops in their district.

how_to_register.in_person: Nearest bank branch, CSC, or Insurance company representative

schemes.follow_up_query_hint: What crops are covered under PMFBY and how do I enroll?

authoritative_source.note: PMFBY Operational Guidelines 2023 — enrolment and premium sharing.

schemes.name: KCC
schemes.one_liner: Short-term crop loan and working capital credit for farmers at an interest-subvented rate (4% effective after prompt repayment).

source.note: KCC is available to all farmers — individual/joint borrowers who are owner cultivators, tenant farmers, oral lessees, sharecroppers, SHGs / JLGs of farmers.
KCC boost when user explicitly asks for credit / loan / KCC / insurance.

required_information.why_needed: The user should be a farmer (owner cultivator, tenant, oral lessee, sharecropper, or member of an SHG / JLG of farmers).
Loan limit is computed on scale of finance × cropped area × crop-specific rate — the crop determines the eligible loan amount.

key_benefits: Interest subvention: 2% below the base rate; additional 3% subvention on prompt repayment (effective 4%)
Short-term crop loan under interest-subvention up to ₹3 lakh
Covers crop production, allied activities (dairy, fisheries), and post-harvest expenses
Also available for animal husbandry, dairy, and fisheries via AHDF-KCC
schemes.who_should_apply: All farmers — owner cultivators, tenant farmers, oral lessees, sharecroppers; SHGs / JLGs of farmers; animal-husbandry, dairy and fisheries operators (via AHDF-KCC).

how_to_register.portal: Any Commercial Bank / Regional Rural Bank / Cooperative Bank branch
how_to_register.in_person: Nearest bank branch — no separate portal required in most cases

schemes.follow_up_query_hint: How do I apply for a Kisan Credit Card at a bank?

authoritative_source.note: RBI KCC Master Circular — eligibility and scheme parameters.

schemes.name: SMAM
schemes.one_liner: Subsidy on the purchase of farm machinery and equipment (rotavators, tractors, Custom Hiring Centres, etc.); enhanced rate for SC/ST, women, small/marginal farmers, and NE-state beneficiaries.

source.note: SMAM targets adoption of farm mechanization and creation of Custom Hiring Centres / Farm Machinery Banks.
Enhanced subsidy rates for SC/ST/OBC beneficiaries.
Enhanced subsidy for small and marginal farmers.

required_information.why_needed: SMAM subsidises specific machinery / CHC components — we need to know what the user wants to buy.
General category (up to 40%) vs SC/ST/small/women/NE (up to 50%) — subsidy % depends on this.
Small/marginal farmers get the enhanced rate.

key_benefits: Enhanced subsidy for SC/ST, women, small/marginal farmers, NE-state beneficiaries
General category: up to 40% of implement cost; enhanced: up to 50%
Establishment of Custom Hiring Centres (CHCs), Farm Machinery Banks (FMBs), and Hi-Tech Hubs
Covers a wide catalog: rotavators, tractors (up to specified HP), sprayers, harvesters, threshers, etc.
schemes.who_should_apply: Individual farmers wanting to buy farm implements at subsidised rates; FPOs, Cooperatives, SHGs wanting to run CHCs / FMBs.

how_to_register.in_person: State Nodal Officer / District Agri Office

schemes.follow_up_query_hint: How do I apply for a single-implement subsidy under SMAM?

authoritative_source.note: SMAM Operational Guidelines — beneficiary categories and subsidy patterns.

schemes.name: MIDH
schemes.long_name: Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture
schemes.one_liner: Financial assistance for horticulture: nurseries, protected cultivation (shade-net / poly-house), cold storage, post-harvest management, and organic certification.

source.note: MIDH targets horticultural crops — fruits, vegetables, flowers, spices, medicinal & aromatic plants.
HMNEH sub-scheme covers all states in NE and Himalayan Region with enhanced pattern.
MIDH covers cold storage, pack-houses, and post-harvest management.

required_information.why_needed: MIDH applies to horticultural crops — we need to know the user is a horticulture farmer or planning a horticulture project.
HMNEH targets NE + Himalayan states with enhanced patterns; plains fall under NHM.
MIDH sub-schemes fund different components — nurseries, protected cultivation, cold storage, organic certification — which one applies?

key_benefits: Subsidy on shade-net houses, poly-houses, tissue-culture plantlets
Cold storage and pack-house support
Enhanced rates for NE and Himalayan states under HMNEH sub-scheme
Sub-schemes: NHM, HMNEH, NHB, CDB, CIH each targeting different beneficiary sets
schemes.who_should_apply: Horticulture farmers, FPOs, and agri-entrepreneurs across sub-schemes: NHM (plains), HMNEH (NE + Himalayan), NHB (commercial horticulture), CDB (coconut), CIH (NE HRD).

how_to_register.in_person: State Horticulture Mission Office or NHB (for commercial projects)

schemes.follow_up_query_hint: What subsidy rate does MIDH provide for a shade-net house?

authoritative_source.note: MIDH Operational Guidelines 2025 — sub-schemes and target groups.

schemes.name: NFSM
schemes.long_name: National Food Security Mission (renamed to NFSNM in 2024-25)
schemes.one_liner: Increases production of rice, wheat, pulses, coarse cereals, nutri-cereals and oilseeds via integrated area demonstrations, seed distribution, and mechanization support.

source.note: NFSM (now NFSNM) targets rice, wheat, pulses, coarse cereals, nutri-cereals and oilseeds; NMEO adds oil palm.

required_information.why_needed: NFSM assistance is per-crop — we need to know which of the target crops the user grows.
State-specific cluster demonstrations — availability depends on the user's state.

key_benefits: Assistance for improved seeds (foundation, certified), integrated nutrient/pest management, and farm mechanization
Cluster-based demonstrations on rice, wheat, pulses, coarse cereals, nutri-cereals, and oilseeds
Renamed to NFSNM in 2024-25 with added focus on nutri-cereals and oil palm (via NMEO)
schemes.who_should_apply: Farmers growing rice / wheat / pulses / coarse cereals / oilseeds / nutri-cereals in states covered by the mission for that crop.

how_to_register.portal: State Agriculture Department / DBT Agriculture portal (state-specific)

schemes.follow_up_query_hint: What is the assistance rate for pulses under NFSM?

authoritative_source.note: NFSM → NFSNM rename notification and scope.

schemes.name: AIF
schemes.one_liner: Medium-to-long-term debt financing (up to ₹2 crore per project, expanded to more categories from Aug 2024) at an interest-subvented rate for post-harvest management and community farming assets.

source.note: AIF finances post-harvest management infrastructure and community farming assets.
AIF Aug 2024 expansion covers cold storage, warehouses, and primary processing.

required_information.why_needed: AIF funds specific infrastructure components — we need to know which project type.
AIF is open to farmers, FPOs, PACS, cooperatives, agri-entrepreneurs — the entity type determines the application route.

key_benefits: Interest subvention: 3% per annum on loans up to ₹2 crore
Credit guarantee cover under CGTMSE
Eligible components: cold storage, warehouses, processing units, community farming assets, custom hiring centres, primary processing
Aug 2024 expansion: farmers, FPOs, PACS, cooperatives, agri-entrepreneurs eligible across more component types
schemes.who_should_apply: Farmers, FPOs, PACS, cooperatives, agri-entrepreneurs, marketing cooperatives, and other eligible entities pursuing infrastructure projects.

how_to_register.in_person: Lending institution (bank / NBFC) partnered with AIF

schemes.follow_up_query_hint: What is the interest subvention rate and maximum loan amount under AIF?

authoritative_source.note: AIF Revised Scheme Guidelines September 2024 — eligibility and terms.
